Subsample BirdNET detections by species

Source: R/birdnet_subsample.R
birdnet_subsample.Rd

Draws a subsample of n detections from a BirdNET output data frame, for example for manual validation. Sampling is done across all rows of data. To subsample one species, filter to that species first (see Examples). Four methods are available: even or proportional stratified sampling across confidence score bins, simple random sampling, or the highest-confidence detections. Optionally saves the subsample to a CSV file.

Usage

birdnet_subsample(
  data,
  n,
  method = c("even_stratified", "proportional_stratified", "random", "top"),
  bin_width = 0.05,
  seed = NULL,
  save_to_file = FALSE,
  file = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing BirdNET output.

n

Integer. Total number of detections to subsample. If data has n or fewer rows, all rows are returned.

method

Character. Subsampling method to use. One of:

"even_stratified"

Samples evenly across confidence score bins. Bins with too few detections contribute all they have, and the remainder is shared among the other bins.

"proportional_stratified"

Samples across confidence score bins in proportion to the number of detections in each bin.

"random"

Simple random sample of n detections.

"top"

The n detections with the highest confidence.

Defaults to "even_stratified".

bin_width

Numeric. Width of the confidence score bins used by the stratified methods. Defaults to 0.05.

seed

Integer or NULL. If given, the subsample is reproducible. The random number generator state of your session is left unchanged.

save_to_file

Logical. If TRUE, saves the output to a CSV file. Defaults to FALSE. Automatically set to TRUE if file is provided.

file

Character or NULL. File path to save the output CSV. If NULL and save_to_file = TRUE, saves as "subsampled_data.csv" in the working directory.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses the status messages about how many detections were returned and whether all of them were kept because data had no more than n rows. Defaults to FALSE.

#' @details Choosing a method.

  • "random" gives an unbiased sample, suited to estimating overall precision.

  • "even_stratified" gives balanced coverage across confidence scores, suited to relating precision to score or choosing a threshold.

  • "proportional_stratified" mirrors the confidence distribution of the detections, so it is dominated by low-confidence detections.

  • "top" is useful for confirming that a species is present, but it is biased for estimating precision.

Several species. Sampling is not done per species. To subsample each species separately, apply the function to each species in turn (see Examples).

Value

A data frame containing the subsampled observations.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# one species: filter first, then subsample
my_data |>
  dplyr::filter(common_name == "Barred Owl") |>
  birdnet_subsample(n = 100, method = "even_stratified", seed = 1)

# several species: apply the function to each one
my_data |>
  split(my_data$common_name) |>
  purrr::map(birdnet_subsample, n = 100) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
} # }
